alternatives.argument: For each node j, the primal pass costs w_j. By the declared bounded local pullback and parent accumulation costs, the reverse work at j is at most (c+ar)w_j because w_j≥1. Summing gives (1+c+ar)W. The stored graph values, cotangents, bounded workspace, and one-step local data occupy O(S) scalar entries under the theorem’s explicit fixed-dimension and cost assumptions. This argument is present in the complete local proof at step 1.1–2.1 and does not use the dropped URL.

The schedule is defined locally as two deterministic procedures. Uniform-block mode saves block-start states, replays each prefix, records one local transition, and reverses it; binomial mode uses the stated capacity recurrence and recursive split. The complete correctness and cost proof is separately authored in thm-checkpointed-reverse-schedules-preserve-adjoints-and-cost-bounds. This local algorithm definition does not depend on the dropped URL.

The binomial construction defines C(d,0)=C(0,t)=1 and splits N steps into L=min(N−1,C(d,t−1)) and R=N−L, so both child intervals satisfy their capacities and are strictly shorter. Deterministic replay and reverse rules are specified in the local algorithm; the schedule’s correctness and all cost bounds are proved in the paired theorem. This gives a complete independently authored account of the cited recursive procedure.

For uniform blocks, induction over deterministic transitions recovers each original primal state, so each replayed local tape is exact and the decreasing block/step order is ordinary reverse order. A block of length r incurs prefix replay lengths r−1,…,0 and hence r(r−1)/2 evaluations. For binomial mode, Pascal recurrence gives C(d,t)=binom(d+t,d); the split has 1≤L<N and R≤C(d−1,t), so recursion terminates. Induction on N proves right-then-left cotangent composition equals the full reverse sweep. The midpoint is one saved state; right recursion uses d−1 more and left recursion uses d after release, so peak is d. Each left-step replay cost is one split replay plus at most t−1 inner replays, while right costs at most t; totals yield the claimed tW additional work. These arguments are fully written in local proof steps 1.1–5.1.

The cost model counts recorded local forward calls separately as What and local reverse calls as Wbar; the unrecorded replay bound is at most t per each transition, so total work is What+Wbar+tW. A state snapshot stack of at most d plus a live state and maximum one-step tape G gives storage G+(d+1)Rs. The local proof steps 3.1–5.1 prove the finite recurrence, snapshot bound, replay count, and cost; no cost claim is borrowed from the inaccessible endpoint.
